thread:
mira: Fyi — noticed similar pattern in last three incidents: inference tails out under sustained bursts. I want concrete postmortem follow-ups that result in tests we can run in CI and during chaos drills. Thinking: expand regression prompt sets, add a bounded load test scenario, and an automated fallback simulation.

ana: +1. can we map each follow-up to a ticket and an owner? otherwise stuff falls through.

todd: I can own the load tests. I propose a stage-level job that ramps qps and asserts p95 latency < 350ms and no 5xx surge. I'll open INF-4298 and sketch the scenario.

kevin: I can take the test harness + CI integration. I'll add a new pipeline step `evals/regression:incidents` that runs nightly against pinned model versions. Will need the prompt sets and expected sanity checks.

mira: Thanks. ana — can you own the prompt set additions? specifically: add the 120 prompts that reproduce the slow-tail behaviour and label expected tokens/outputs where meaningful. Ticket INF-4299. Target: 1 week.

ana: I can do that. I'll sample from logs (s3://redwood-prod/logs/inference/slow-tail/) and the incident prompt dumps. Will list sources in the ticket.

ops-bot: New issue created: INF-4298 by todd — "stage load test: sustained bursts & p95 assertion"

ops-bot: New issue created: INF-4299 by ana — "regression prompt set: slow-tail reproduction (120 prompts)"

mira: Also want a chaos drill variant: simulate a partial KV cache miss + slightly higher seq lengths to force different kernel paths. Run monthly and include checklist to validate fallback routing. Who's up for owning drill runbook?

todd: I can draft the runbook and schedule the first drill next month. We'll include a playbook snippet and a run command like:
```
# run rough burst with wrk (example)
wrk -t12 -c200 -d10m --latency http://stage-redwood/api/v1/generate -s scripts/long_seq.lua
```
We'll also simulate KV eviction by restarting cache pods on a subset of hosts.

kevin: For the automated fallback simulation, I'll add a synthetic test that toggles model variants via the routing config and asserts no error-rate spike. Will need a mock of the fallback table. Ticket INF-4300. ETA 2 weeks.

ana: Quick Q re: expected outputs — for prompts where we only check latency patterns we should avoid brittle token-level assertions. We'll add coarse-grained sanity checks (e.g., prefixes, safe regex, length ranges).

mira: Agreed. Make two categories on the prompt set ticket: "latency-sensitive" (no token asserts) and "regression-sensitive" (token-level / semantic checks).

todd: Putting timeline in INF-4298: prototype load job in 3 days, staging job in 7 days, run smoke + record baseline in 10 days.

kevin: INF-4300 created. I'll attach the mock routing config and a small harness.

ana: INF-4299 draft created with 120 prompts and categories. PR will follow later today.

mira: Great. Two more things: 1) link these tickets from the original postmortem (PM-2910) so we can track closure; 2) add an "owner review" line item in the next all-hands ops sync for accountability.

todd: Done — linked INF-4298 to PM-2910.

ops-bot: Linked INF-4298 -> PM-2910; INF-4299 -> PM-2910; INF-4300 -> PM-2910

kevin: I'll add a small dashboard in Console: tests/regression-incidents with pass/fail and p95/mean latency over time. Can use that in the monthly drill review.

mira: Perfect. Can everyone add realistic test data and a short runbook snippet to their tickets so reviewers can reproduce? keep notes in the ticket under "repro steps".

ana: will do. PR incoming. :+1:

todd: starting the load test thread in the infra repo now. ping me if you want in on the scenario design. :memo:

kevin: I'll wire up CI jobs and the dashboard tile. target to have all green by the next ops sync (two weeks).

mira: Thanks all. I'll mark these as action items in the postmortem and set a follow-up check-in in 2 weeks. :eyes:
